Here is the complete documentation of the `tutors.json` course file format.

---

## 1. Complete JSON Structure

The file at `D:\code\tutors\test-course\tutors.json` is the sole `tutors.json` file in this repository. The structure is a recursive tree of Learning Objects (LOs). Every node in the tree shares a common base shape, and certain types extend it.

### Base Lo (Learning Object) -- every node

Every learning object at every level contains these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `route` | `string` | URL path with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder, e.g. `"/course/{{COURSEURL}}"` |
| `type` | `string` | One of: `course`, `topic`, `unit`, `side`, `note`, `talk`, `lab`, `tutorial`, `archive`, `web`, `github`, `panelnote`, `paneltalk`, `panelvideo`, `podcast`, `notebook` |
| `title` | `string` | Display title |
| `summary` | `string` | Short description (markdown allowed) |
| `contentMd` | `string` | Full markdown content (raw markdown string with `\n` newlines) |
| `frontMatter` | `object` | Key-value pairs parsed from YAML front matter. May be empty `{}` |
| `id` | `string` | Identifier unique within its parent, e.g. `"topic-01-mermaid"`, `"unit-1"`, `"note-1-flowchart"` |
| `img` | `string` | Image URL with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder, or `""` if none. At runtime becomes e.g. `"https://example.netlify.app/img/logo.png"` |
| `imgFile` | `string` | Local image filename, or `""` |
| `video` | `string` | Video URL with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder, or `""` |
| `videoids` | `object` | `{ "videoid": string, "videoIds": VideoIdentifier[] }` where each VideoIdentifier is `{ "service": string, "id": string, "url"?: string, "externalUrl"?: string }` |
| `hide` | `boolean` | Whether to hide this LO from display |
| `authLevel` | `number` | Authentication level required (0 = public) |

### Composite Lo (course, topic, unit, side) -- extends base

Composite types have an additional field:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `los` | `Lo[]` | Array of child learning objects (recursive) |

At runtime these are also decorated with `panels`, `units`, `toc`, but these are not in the JSON -- they are computed during tree decoration.

### Course-level (top-level object) -- extends Composite

The root object additionally carries:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `properties` | `Properties` | Dictionary of `string -> string` (or nested objects). Known keys include: `credits`, `slack`, `zoom`, `moodle`, `youtube`, `teams`, `podcast`, `companions`, `portfolio`, `llm`, `private`, `hideVideos`, `footer`, `labStepsAutoNumber`, `auth`, `defaultPdfReader`, `pdfOrientation`, `ignorepin`, `icon` |
| `calendar` | `Properties` (optional) | Calendar data with `title` and `weeks` array. See section 7 below |
| `enrollment` | `Enrollment` (optional) | Enrollment whitelist. See section 7 below |

These fields are defined in the type but not present in the test-course JSON (which has only `properties.credits`).

### Talk / PanelTalk -- extends base

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `pdf` | `string` | PDF URL with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder |
| `pdfFile` | `string` | Local PDF filename, or `""` |

### Lab -- extends base

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `los` | `LabStep[]` | Array of lab steps (not recursive LOs) |
| `pdf` | `string` | PDF URL with placeholder |
| `pdfFile` | `string` | Local PDF filename |

Each `LabStep` has: `{ title, shortTitle, contentMd, contentHtml?, route, id, type }`.

### Archive -- extends base

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `archiveFile` | `string` | Filename of the downloadable archive, e.g. `"course.zip"` |

### Tutorial -- extends base

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `pdf` | `string` | PDF URL with placeholder |
| `pdfFile` | `string` | Local PDF filename |

### Podcast -- extends base

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `episode` | `{ service: string, id: string }` | Podcast episode identifier |

### Note, Web, Github, PanelNote, PanelVideo -- extend base only

No additional JSON fields beyond the base Lo.

### Notebook -- extends base

A notebook LO has additional fields not in the formal TypeScript `Lo` type but used via `as any` casting:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `cells` | `NotebookCell[]` | Array of notebook cells |
| `kernelLanguage` | `string` | Language of the notebook kernel, defaults to `"python"` |

See section 3 below for cell structure.

---

## 2. FrontMatter Structure for Marp Slides

The `frontMatter` field is a `Properties` dictionary (`{ [key: string]: string }`). For Marp presentations, the test-course shows:

```json
"frontMatter": { "marp": "true" }
```

The content in `contentMd` for a Marp talk contains the full YAML front matter block:

```
---
marp: true
theme: default
paginate: true
---

# Slide Title
...
---
## Next Slide
```

Detection logic is in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\marp-renderer.ts`:
- `isMarpContent()` returns true if `frontMatter.marp` is `true` or `"true"`, or if contentMd starts with `---\nmarp: true`
- `buildMarpMarkdown()` reconstructs the full marp markdown by prepending a front matter block if one is missing, using `frontMatter.theme` and `frontMatter.paginate` if present
- Other recognized frontMatter keys: `order` (for sorting LOs), `icon` (with `{ type, color }` sub-object for custom icons)

---

## 3. Notebook Cell Structure

Defined in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\ui\learning-objects\content\Notebook.svelte`:

### NotebookCell

```typescript
interface NotebookCell {
  cellType: "markdown" | "code" | "raw";   // Type of cell
  source: string;                           // Raw source content
  sourceHtml?: string;                      // Computed at runtime, not in JSON
  outputs: NotebookOutput[];                // Array of cell outputs
  outputsHtml?: string;                     // Computed at runtime, not in JSON
  executionCount: number | null;            // Execution counter (null if not executed)
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;        // Cell metadata dictionary
  id: string;                               // Cell identifier
}
```

### NotebookOutput

```typescript
interface NotebookOutput {
  outputType: "stream" | "execute_result" | "display_data" | "error";
  text?: string;             // For "stream" outputs
  data?: Record<string, string>;  // MIME-type keyed data for execute_result/display_data
                                   // Keys: "text/html", "image/svg+xml", "image/png",
                                   //        "image/jpeg", "text/latex", "text/plain"
  traceback?: string[];      // For "error" outputs
  name?: string;             // Stream name ("stdout" or "stderr")
  executionCount?: number | null;
}
```

### kernelLanguage

The `kernelLanguage` field on the notebook LO (default `"python"`) is used by `convertNotebookToHtml()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\markdown\services\markdown.svelte.ts` to wrap code cells in fenced code blocks for syntax highlighting:

```typescript
const fenced = "```" + kernelLang + "\n" + (cell.source || "") + "\n```";
```

---

## 4. Markdown Content: contentMd vs contentHtml

- **`contentMd`** is stored in the JSON file. It contains raw markdown with embedded newlines as `\n` characters.
- **`contentHtml`** is NOT stored in the JSON. It is computed at runtime during "tree decoration" by `convertLoToHtml()`.
- For most LO types, conversion happens immediately during `decorateCourseTree()`.
- For `lab`, `note`, and `notebook` types, conversion is deferred to on-demand loading (see `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts` line 78-79) to avoid the cost of converting all at once.
- The `filter()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\markdown-utils.ts` rewrites relative image paths (`img/`) and archive paths to absolute URLs using the course URL before conversion.

---

## 5. How Images/Icons Are Referenced

### Images in JSON
- `img` field contains a URL with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder: e.g. `"https://{{COURSEURL}}/img/logo.png"`. Can be `""` if no image.
- `imgFile` stores the bare filename.
- During `injectCourseUrl()`, `{{COURSEURL}}` in `img` is replaced with the **courseUrl** (the domain, e.g. `"test-course.netlify.app"`), producing `"https://test-course.netlify.app/img/logo.png"`.

### Icons
- Icons can be set via `frontMatter.icon` as `{ "type": "iconify-id", "color": "tailwind-color" }`. The `loadIcon()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\lo-utils.ts` extracts this.
- Course-level icons can also be set via `properties.icon` with the same `{ type, color }` shape.
- Default icons per LO type come from icon theme files like `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\themes\icons\fluent-icons.ts`. Icons use [Iconify](https://iconify.design/) identifiers (e.g. `"fluent:beaker-24-filled"`, `"simple-icons:jupyter"`, `"mdi:github"`).

---

## 6. Route Format and {{COURSEURL}} Usage

### Route patterns in JSON

| LO Type | Route Pattern |
|---------|--------------|
| course | `/course/{{COURSEURL}}` |
| topic | `/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id` |
| unit | `/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/parent-topic-id/` (note trailing slash) |
| note | `/note/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/note-id` |
| talk | `/talk/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/talk-id` |
| lab | `/lab/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/lab-id` |
| archive | `/archive/{{COURSEURL}}` (transformed to full URL with archiveFile) |
| video | `/video/{{COURSEURL}}/...` |
| notebook | `/notebook/{{COURSEURL}}/...` |

### Replacement logic (`injectCourseUrl()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts`)

- `route`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseId** (e.g. `"test-course"`)
- `img`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseUrl** (e.g. `"test-course.netlify.app"`)
- `video`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseId**
- `pdf` (talks, labs, tutorials): `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseUrl**
- `archive`: Route is fully rewritten to `https://{courseUrl}/{archiveFile}`

The distinction between courseId (used for routing) and courseUrl (used for asset fetching) is handled by `determineCourseUrl()`:
- Plain IDs like `"test-course"` become courseUrl `"test-course.netlify.app"`
- Full URLs are used as-is
- Localhost/IP addresses use `http://` protocol

---

## 7. Calendar, Companion, and Enrollment Data

### Calendar

The `calendar` field is a `Properties` object at the course level in the JSON. Its expected structure (parsed in `initCalendar()` in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\course-utils.ts`):

```json
{
  "calendar": {
    "title": "Semester Schedule",
    "weeks": [
      { "2024-01-15": { "title": "Week 1: Introduction", "type": "standard" } },
      { "2024-01-22": { "title": "Week 2: Basics", "type": "standard" } },
      { "2024-01-29": { "title": "Reading Week", "type": "break" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each week entry is an object with a date key mapping to `{ title, type }`. At runtime these are converted to `WeekType` objects with a `dateObj: Date` field, and the `currentWeek` is computed. The course gets `hasCalendar: true` when this field exists.

### Companions

Companions are NOT a JSON field -- they are computed from `properties` at runtime by `createCompanions()`. The `properties` object can contain these known companion keys:

- `slack` -- URL to Slack channel
- `zoom` -- URL to Zoom meeting
- `moodle` -- URL to Moodle page
- `youtube` -- URL to YouTube channel
- `teams` -- URL to Teams meeting
- `podcast` -- URL to podcast

Additionally, a `properties.companions` nested object can define custom companions:
```json
{
  "properties": {
    "slack": "https://app.slack.com/...",
    "companions": {
      "discord": { "link": "https://discord.gg/...", "title": "Discord Server", "icon": "logos:discord-icon" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Enrollment

The `enrollment` field is optional at the course level. Its TypeScript type (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\calendar-types.ts`):

```typescript
type Student = {
  name: string;
  id: string;
};

type Enrollment = {
  whitelist: string[];       // List of authorized identifiers
  students: Student[];       // List of student records
};
```

When `course.enrollment` exists, `hasEnrollment` is set to `true`.

---

## 4. Markdown Content: contentMd vs contentHtml

- **`contentMd`** is stored in the JSON file. It contains raw markdown with embedded newlines as `\n` characters.
- **`contentHtml`** is NOT stored in the JSON. It is computed at runtime during "tree decoration" by `convertLoToHtml()`.
- For most LO types, conversion happens immediately during `decorateCourseTree()`.
- For `lab`, `note`, and `notebook` types, conversion is deferred to on-demand loading (see `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts` line 78-79) to avoid the cost of converting all at once.
- The `filter()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\markdown-utils.ts` rewrites relative image paths (`img/`) and archive paths to absolute URLs using the course URL before conversion.

## 5. How Images/Icons Are Referenced

### Images in JSON
- `img` field contains a URL with `{{COURSEURL}}` placeholder: e.g. `"https://{{COURSEURL}}/img/logo.png"`. Can be `""` if no image.
- `imgFile` stores the bare filename.
- During `injectCourseUrl()`, `{{COURSEURL}}` in `img` is replaced with the **courseUrl** (the domain, e.g. `"test-course.netlify.app"`), producing `"https://test-course.netlify.app/img/logo.png"`.

### Icons
- Icons can be set via `frontMatter.icon` as `{ "type": "iconify-id", "color": "tailwind-color" }`. The `loadIcon()` function in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\lo-utils.ts` extracts this.
- Course-level icons can also be set via `properties.icon` with the same `{ type, color }` shape.
- Default icons per LO type come from icon theme files like `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\themes\icons\fluent-icons.ts`. Icons use [Iconify](https://iconify.design/) identifiers (e.g. `"fluent:beaker-24-filled"`, `"simple-icons:jupyter"`, `"mdi:github"`).

## 6. Route Format and {{COURSEURL}} Usage

### Route patterns in JSON

| LO Type | Route Pattern |
|---------|--------------|
| course | `/course/{{COURSEURL}}` |
| topic | `/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id` |
| unit | `/topic/{{COURSEURL}}/parent-topic-id/` (note trailing slash) |
| note | `/note/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/note-id` |
| talk | `/talk/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/talk-id` |
| lab | `/lab/{{COURSEURL}}/topic-id/unit-id/lab-id` |
| archive | `/archive/{{COURSEURL}}` (transformed to full URL with archiveFile) |
| video | `/video/{{COURSEURL}}/...` |
| notebook | `/notebook/{{COURSEURL}}/...` |

### Replacement logic (`injectCourseUrl()` in `D:\code\tutors\src\lib\services\course\services\lo-tree.ts`)

- `route`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseId** (e.g. `"test-course"`)
- `img`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseUrl** (e.g. `"test-course.netlify.app"`)
- `video`: `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseId**
- `pdf` (talks, labs, tutorials): `{{COURSEURL}}` is replaced with the **courseUrl**
- `archive`: Route is fully rewritten to `https://{courseUrl}/{archiveFile}`

The distinction between courseId (used for routing) and courseUrl (used for asset fetching) is handled by `determineCourseUrl()`:
- Plain IDs like `"test-course"` become courseUrl `"test-course.netlify.app"`
- Full URLs are used as-is
- Localhost/IP addresses use `http://` protocol

## 7. Calendar, Companion, and Enrollment Data

### Calendar

The `calendar` field is a `Properties` object at the course level in the JSON. Its expected structure (parsed in `initCalendar()` in `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\utils\course-utils.ts`):

```json
{
  "calendar": {
    "title": "Semester Schedule",
    "weeks": [
      { "2024-01-15": { "title": "Week 1: Introduction", "type": "standard" } },
      { "2024-01-22": { "title": "Week 2: Basics", "type": "standard" } },
      { "2024-01-29": { "title": "Reading Week", "type": "break" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each week entry is an object with a date key mapping to `{ title, type }`. At runtime these are converted to `WeekType` objects with a `dateObj: Date` field, and the `currentWeek` is computed. The course gets `hasCalendar: true` when this field exists.

### Companions

Companions are NOT a JSON field -- they are computed from `properties` at runtime by `createCompanions()`. The `properties` object can contain these known companion keys:

- `slack` -- URL to Slack channel
- `zoom` -- URL to Zoom meeting
- `moodle` -- URL to Moodle page
- `youtube` -- URL to YouTube channel
- `teams` -- URL to Teams meeting
- `podcast` -- URL to podcast

Additionally, a `properties.companions` nested object can define custom companions:
```json
{
  "properties": {
    "slack": "https://app.slack.com/...",
    "companions": {
      "discord": { "link": "https://discord.gg/...", "title": "Discord Server", "icon": "logos:discord-icon" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Enrollment

The `enrollment` field is optional at the course level. Its TypeScript type (from `D:\code\tutors\node_modules\@tutors\tutors-model-lib\src\types\calendar-types.ts`):

```typescript
type Student = {
  name: string;
  id: string;
};

type Enrollment = {
  whitelist: string[];       // List of authorized identifiers
  students: Student[];       // List of student records
};
```

When `course.enrollment` exists, `hasEnrollment` is set to `true`.
